f1.quote: Atmospheric plasma spraying was used to deposit an approximately 150 µm-thick AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating on SS316L

f2.quote: followed by 2 h furnace annealing at 400, 550, 700, or 850 °C. The 550 °C condition was selected for corrosion testing because it produced the best reported microstructure and microhardness.

f3.quote: Electrochemical testing used 3.5 wt% H2SO4 with saturated calomel reference and Pt counter electrodes.

f4.quote: Hot-corrosion testing was conducted at 900 °C for ten 5 h cycles (50 h total) under mixture A (75% Na2SO4/25% NaCl), B (70% Na2SO4/20% NaCl/10% V2O5), or C (60% Na2SO4/20% NaCl/20% V2O5).

f9.quote: Relative to uncoated SS316L and the as-sprayed coating, the AlCoCrFeNi-coated specimen annealed at 550 °C should exhibit greater microhardness... Annealing above 550 °C should reduce hardness

f11.quote: higher electrochemical polarization resistance and lower corrosion current
